Threat / vulnerability: A vulnerability in OpenCanary, Twisted, the container runtime or the OS lets one of the constant internet attackers break out of the fake services
The admin SSH key or the laptop that holds it is compromised, giving full control of the VM
Open treatment: Bring the laptop to a supported and patched operating system; resolve disk encryption (SoA 8.1; 7.9)

Threat / vulnerability: Phishing or a reused password gives an attacker the GitHub or Oracle account, to tamper with the demo, the code or the VM
Full attacker addresses or attempted passwords published or leaked from raw logs, a GDPR breach
Usernames, paths and commands sent by attackers contain script that runs in the browsers of people viewing the tracker
Oracle reclaims the idle Always Free VM, an outage, or resource exhaustion breaks links already shared with recruiters
Open treatment: Confirm scheduled monitoring runs (internal audit NC-02); upgrade Oracle to Pay As You Go (SoA 5.23); rebuild drill (SoA 5.30)

Threat / vulnerability: A bug duplicates, drops or misclassifies events, so figures quoted in the CV or on LinkedIn are wrong
A supplier such as the sslip.io name service is flagged as unsafe or fails, blocking the links people click
Open treatment: Replace sslip.io with a custom domain (internal audit OFI-02)

Threat / vulnerability: A malicious or vulnerable package, base image or GitHub Action reaches the service through an update
Floods of requests to the public API or too many live viewers exhaust the 1 GB VM
Processing attacker addresses without a documented basis or retention, or using datasets and databases against their licence terms
The repository is deleted or overwritten, or the laptop is lost, so the service cannot be rebuilt or its evidence shown
